velocity_note: THE COMPUTED FIGURE READS 72/72/0 AND THAT IS NOT THE HONEST STORY. The sprint was PLANNED AT 77 POINTS ACROSS 20 ITEMS. SEO-04 (5pt) parked at its own sourcing gate and was moved to the backlog before close, per the carry-forward rule — and moving it out is what turned 72-of-77 into a flattering 100%. Both numbers belong in the record: 19 of 20 items shipped, 72 of 77 planned points delivered, and the 20th produced a decision not to build rather than a deliverable. A tracker that computes velocity cannot be typed into, which is the point — but it can still be flattered by moving an item, and that is worth knowing about the mechanism.
sizing_accuracy: Sizing held across the board; nothing was narrowed and nothing ran over its estimate. The sprint GREW instead — from the 29 points the owner first approved to 77, in four documented increments: the UX review added 13 (UX-01..04), the SEO review added 5 (RISK-06, SEO-06), finishing Tier 1 added 21 (CONT-05..08 replacing a 4-point placeholder), and the cover work added 3 (CONT-09). Every increment came from evidence produced after approval, and every one was flagged back to the owner rather than absorbed. That is the growth pattern to keep. The one item that did not deliver, SEO-04, was not mis-sized — its gate fired, which is what the gate was for.

learnings.finding: A GLOBAL AUTH EVENT STALLS THE ENTIRE FLEET AND REPORTS AS SUCCESS. The fleet froze four times in one night — once on a usage limit that set a private 4:30am countdown, three times on login expiry. A `/login` in the orchestrator's session does not reach dispatched agents; each is a separate process holding its own credentials. Worse, the status board shows a stalled agent as `IDLE/DONE`, the exact string a finished agent shows. Two agents sat dead for TWO HOURS before anyone noticed, and at one point eight items read as complete when not one had finished.
learnings.why: Marking those eight done on that reading is precisely the failure the ship check exists to prevent. The tell is CLUSTERING: several agents going quiet inside one short window is not simultaneous completion. resume-fleet.sh interrupts and resumes only terminals showing an auth banner and leaves working agents untouched; on its first dry run it also found six agents in OTHER projects stalled on the same expiry that nobody was watching.

learnings.finding: THE DISPATCH LAUNCHER WAS NAMED AFTER THE AGENT, SO CONCURRENT DISPATCHES SILENTLY SHARED ONE BRIEF. `dispatch-agent.ps1` wrote `$env:TEMP/hellokahwin-dispatch/$Agent.ps1`. Three concurrent BMAD dispatches all wrote `BMAD.ps1`; the last write won, and UX-01 and PLAT-09 both came up running PLAT-06's brief. Three agents, one item, and NO ERROR ANYWHERE — distinct handles, clean dispatch output. Only the post-dispatch brief audit caught it.
learnings.why: The launcher is now `$Agent--$briefTag--$timestamp.ps1`, verified by re-running the exact failing case (two concurrent BMAD dispatches, 2/2 correct). THIS IS VERY LIKELY THE TRUE CAUSE OF SPRINT 01'S DUPLICATE DISPATCH, which was diagnosed at the time as the CEO assigning handles by status-board order. That diagnosis produced a genuinely useful fix — capture the handle at dispatch — but it was treating a symptom while the mechanism sat in the launcher. A correct-looking fix for the wrong cause hides the real one.

learnings.finding: THE SHIP CHECK HAD A FALSE NEGATIVE. `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> origin/main` returns false FOREVER for a squash-merged branch, because squashing creates a new commit and the branch tip never becomes an ancestor. The CEO used it on PLAT-05 and reported shipped work as unshipped.
learnings.why: A false negative is worse than no check, because the correct response to 'unshipped' is to ship it again. Verify by CONTENT on the default branch — `git cat-file -e origin/main:<a file the work added>` — and check which merge style the repo uses before trusting either test. The same section now also warns that checking for the WRONG FILENAME is not the same as the thing being absent: a PLAT-06 check reported 'no backlinks migration' because it grepped for `backlink`; the file is `document_links.sql`.

learnings.finding: A RULE WRITTEN THIS SPRINT WAS APPLIED TO THE OPTION IT KILLED AND EXEMPTED THE OPTION THAT REPLACED IT. The SERP-ownership rule — pick targets on volume AND who owns position 1 — was used to kill council halls (blocked by DBKL's own DR 64 booking portal) and then NOT applied to commercial venues, which have their own brand sites above them for exactly the same reason. SEO-04's retrospective found this in the CEO's own rule.
learnings.why: Corrected with a new rule: RESOLVE THE OPERATOR BEFORE YOU RANK A COMPETITOR. The general lesson is sharper than the specific one — a rule that eliminates an option must be run against the replacement before the replacement is adopted, or the rule has only been used to justify a decision already made.

learnings.finding: AGENTS CORRECTED THE CEO REPEATEDLY AND WERE RIGHT EVERY TIME. UX-01 could not reproduce the CEO's '34 of 43 clicks' figure (GSC returns 2 clicks over 28 days) and confirmed the SHAPE instead of restating a number it had not measured — the CEO had quoted that figure all evening without re-deriving it. SEO-05 rejected two of the CEO's five title targets and chose different pages by per-query breakdown. CONT-07 retracted a false SEO claim in its own log unprompted. PLAT-06's agent refused to commit into a checkout another agent was using.
learnings.why: This is now the second sprint running in which the team disproved the CEO more often than the reverse. The standing expectation already says the evidence wins; what this sprint adds is that the CORRECTIONS ARRIVE INSIDE DELIVERABLES — in a work-done log, in a chosen target list — rather than as escalations. So they are only found by reading the report properly, which means a skimmed report costs more than a slow one.

learnings.finding: THE CEO'S OWN VERIFICATION FAILED IN THE SAME SHAPE THREE TIMES: checking the wrong thing and reading the result as an answer. Grepped `backlink` when the file was `document_links.sql`. Guessed article slugs and got 404s instead of reading the agent's own work-done log. Counted pillar empty states with `grep -o`, which matched one rendered block twice and reported 2 where there was 1.
learnings.why: Every one was recoverable because it was checked twice, but each first reading was confidently wrong. The rule added: when a check returns a surprising ABSENCE, verify the check before believing the absence — enumerate what exists rather than asserting what does not.

learnings.finding: run-stats.py PRODUCED AN EMPTY CARD FOR THE SECOND SPRINT RUNNING. It keys off `/buildit`'s ship-log, and a sprint never writes one, so effort per stage is unmeasured for Sprint 01 AND Sprint 02.
learnings.why: Carried forward once already and not acted on, which by the retro's own rule means the template is wrong rather than the run. Twice is the signal. Either `/startsprint` writes the ship-log entry the tool expects, or `run-stats.py` learns to key off a sprint — but 'report it honestly as empty' is not a third acceptable outcome for a third sprint.

learnings.finding: THE GATE THAT KILLS AN ITEM IS A DELIVERABLE, AND IT WORKED. SEO-04's DoD opened with a one-hour sourcing check explicitly allowed to stop the item. It fired: no way to source real venue prices and capacities at scale. The agent built NOTHING — /dewan/ returns 404, zero sitemap entries, zero route files — and did not invent capacities or quietly downgrade back to council halls, both of which the brief named as forbidden.
learnings.why: On a site whose entire competitive claim is that its numbers carry sources, a directory of plausible invented capacities would have been the worst possible outcome and the hardest to detect later. Writing a gate that is allowed to kill the item — and saying so in the DoD — is now the pattern for any item whose value depends on data we do not yet hold.

learnings.finding: A REPRODUCTION IS A STATEMENT ABOUT CONDITIONS, NOT ABOUT A PAGE. RISK-06's agent reproduced a stale-shell symptom on 50 of 61 pages that the CEO could not reproduce at all — because the CEO's own earlier requests had warmed the cache. 'Could not reproduce' was true and told us nothing.
learnings.why: Reading the source for a mechanism first is what made 50/61 appear on the first try. The same class of error nearly shipped in RISK-05, whose monitor initially treated a FAILED inspection as 'absent' and would have reported clean over a shrinking denominator — SEO-01's failure re-implemented one layer up. Both were caught by asking what the measurement could not see.

process_findings: THE PROCESS HELD WHERE SPRINT 01 BROKE, AND BROKE SOMEWHERE NEW. Sprint 01's defining failure was three items marked done without shipping, all found by the owner asking. THAT DID NOT RECUR: every one of the 19 completed items was verified against production or against content on the default branch before being marked, and the ship check caught real problems four separate times — PLAT-06 finished but 6 commits unpushed and 7 ahead of main, SEO-05 finished with 11 site commits unpushed, four unpushed commits across two trees after wave 1, and six unpushed docs commits on the final sweep. In every case the CEO pushed and merged rather than marking done. PLAT-08 was REOPENED after self-marking done on a preview URL that returned 302 rather than the claimed 200. WHAT BROKE INSTEAD WAS ORCHESTRATION, NOT VERIFICATION: four auth stalls that read as success, a dispatch launcher collision that put three agents on one item, and a ship-check false negative that called shipped work unshipped. All three are now fixed in the tools rather than in anyone's memory, which is the correct place — Murat's Sprint 01 line still governs: a gate you have to remember is a suggestion. ORDERING WORKED: risk items ran first and the content gate (RISK-04) shipped before a single one of the 25 articles was written, so nothing published into the void that Sprint 01 published into. Dependencies were declared in the briefs and held — SEO-06 landed before CONT-05 and CONT-07 wrote into its cluster, UX-01 released the site files before UX-02/03/04 touched them, and PLAT-05 merged before PLAT-09 added /docs to the sidebar. THE OWNER WAS NEVER THE CRITICAL PATH except where they should have been: PLAT-08's PR that would deploy the live public site at 2am was deliberately left open for them, and the photographer outreach that CONT-09's escalation depends on is theirs by design.
carried_forward: SEO-04 (backlog, 5pt) — venue entity pages. Parked at its own sourcing gate: we cannot source real prices and capacities at scale. Its own recommendation is the way in: PHONE-VERIFY eight venues and publish with 'disemak Ogos 2026', which is the method that built mas-kahwin-ikut-negeri and is our actual differentiator. That is field research in Malay and needs a CONTENT owner, not an engineering dispatch.

OPEN, unowned: SIX SITEMAP URLs ARE SERVED WITH noindex and Google crawled and excluded all six. Found by RISK-05, which correctly recorded it and did not half-fix it because it met neither of its own alarm conditions. src/app/sitemap.ts.

OPEN, owner-only: hellokahwin PR #4 carries the preview banner and is deliberately left OPEN — merging it deploys the live public site. PLAT-08's agent stopped and asked rather than shipping it unasked at 2am, and the CEO agreed.

OPEN: previews are Vercel-SSO-gated, so they work for the OWNER and not for the CEO. Turning deployment protection off would make every preview publicly readable, which is a secret-exposure decision nobody has asked for. The honest position is that 'show me before you ship' now works for the owner only.

CARRIED FROM SPRINT 01, still open: cold renders take 5–22s against a route declaring maxDuration=5. RISK-06 and RISK-04 changed what Googlebot meets first and RISK-05 now watches it, so Sprint 03 can revisit this with the monitor's data rather than by guessing.
